Validate the Whole Pipeline by Truncating Pigs

Source: R/validate_truncation.R
validate_truncation.Rd

Remove all visits of part of the pigs over some days of the stage (late entry, early exit or a gap), rerun the pipeline from clean_weight() to calc_fcr() with each QC setting, and compare ADG, ADFI and FCR with the result of all data. Nothing of the hidden days is used, so the result measures what really happens when a pig misses these days.

validate_truncation(
  visits,
  settings = qc_config(),
  scenarios = c("late10", "late20", "early10", "early20", "gap10"),
  share = 0.5,
  reps = 5,
  top = 0.2,
  pigs = NULL,
  seed = 1,
  verbose = 1,
  cores = 1
)

Arguments

visits

Result of prep_visits().

settings

A QC object from qc_config(), or a named list of them to compare, e.g. list(lm = qc_config(impute_method = "loess_lm"), pop = qc_config()).

scenarios

Days removed, counted on the stage of the first setting (from its full-data run):

  • "late<d>": the first d days of the stage and everything before (late entry), e.g. "late20";

  • "early<d>": the last d days of the stage and everything after (early exit);

  • "gap<d>": d consecutive days in the middle of the stage.

share

Share of the pigs truncated in one run (default 0.5). The pigs are split at random into round(1 / share) groups, each group is truncated in turn, so every pig is truncated once per repetition.

reps

Number of repetitions, each with a new random split. Default 5.

top

Share of the best pigs for the selection agreement top_agree (default 0.2: the best 20%). Best = highest ADG, lowest FCR, highest ADFI.

pigs

Pigs to truncate. Default NULL: pigs whose stage is fully covered by records in the first setting (adg_type == "observed") and that have an FCR.

seed

Random seed.

verbose

0 (silent) or 1 (progress, default).

cores

Number of CPU cores: runs of the pipeline in parallel.

Value

A list of class ppt_validation with

  • summary: one row per setting, scenario and trait (adg, adfi, fcr): the mean over repetitions of bias (truncated - full), rmse, mae_pct (mean absolute error, % of the full value), pearson and spearman correlation with the full value, slope of the regression of the truncated on the full value (below 1: the differences between pigs shrink), top_agree (share of the best top pigs on full data that are also among the best after truncation), n (pigs with both values) and n_lost (pigs that lost their value); columns ending in _sd give the SD over repetitions;

  • per_rep: the same measures for every repetition;

  • per_pig: full and truncated value of every pig, trait, setting, scenario and repetition;

  • settings.

Details

The reference is the result of all data with the same setting, not the unknown true value: the measures tell how stable a setting is when data are missing, which is what matters to compare settings. With few pigs (e.g. 20), differences of a few hundredths in a correlation are noise; look at the _sd columns and use more repetitions.

Pigs whose test becomes too short after truncation (e.g. below min_test_days) are removed by clean_weight() and counted in n_lost.

See also

validate_adfi(), validate_adg() for faster checks of single steps.

Examples

visits <- prep_visits(nedap, verbose = 0)
# 2 settings x 1 scenario x 1 repetition; use more repetitions on real data
res <- validate_truncation(
  visits,
  settings = list(lm = qc_config(impute_method = "loess_lm"), pop = qc_config()),
  scenarios = "late20", reps = 1
)
#>

#> [2/2] Truncated runs ■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■ 2/4 | ETA  2s
